pixel_convention: x right, y down, origin at top-left pixel; time t = frame / 60

camera.evidence: phase correlation of frame 0 vs frame 95 over the house region: shift (-0.009, -0.006) px; mean abs pixel difference 1.3 grey levels
camera.perspective: front-on, roughly eye-level view of the house; no usable vanishing lines. Treated as a 2D scene: the bird flies in a plane roughly parallel to the image plane (bird apparent size roughly constant, bbox_w ~35 px throughout)

objects.name: bird
objects.description: the only moving object: a small dark-backed bird with a light belly, head pointing right, flapping its wings. Flies left to right across the sky above the house in an arc (rises, then descends).
objects.reference_point: ref_x/ref_y = centroid of the 3x3-eroded mask (body centre, wing tips have little weight); centroid_x/y and bbox_cx/cy given as alternatives (they agree to ~1-2 px)

bbox_w_px.note: minimum 21-26 px only in frames 8-16 when the bird is over the white sun and its pale parts are lost; outside the sun 34-40 px

pixel_size_summary_frames_4_99.wingspan_note: wings mostly seen side-on; vertical extent (bbox_h) ranges 16-35 px outside the sun frames; horizontal extent (bbox_w) 34-40 px

path_summary.end: frame 99 at ref ~(1729.2, 299.8), still in frame, descending to the right
